brief.t: Founded in Lahore in 1894 with Lala Lajpat Rai among its early leaders; now headquartered in New Delhi.
A public sector bank: the Government of India owns about 70% of its shares.
Led by MD & CEO Ashok Chandra since 16 January 2025.
Record FY 2025-26 net profit of ₹16,904 crore; Gross NPA fell to 2.95% from 3.95%.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit rose 12.8% to ₹5,532 crore; Gross NPA improved further to 2.55%.

timeline.t: Incorporated in Lahore; opened for business in April 1895.
Registered office moved from Lahore to Delhi after Partition.
Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India merged into PNB.
Ashok Chandra took charge as MD & CEO.

model.how: PNB earns mainly from the gap between interest on loans and interest paid on deposits, plus fees. As a public sector bank it also runs many government schemes, farm lending and financial-inclusion work.
flow: Bank lends to people, farmers, MSMEs and companies

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Government of India (as main owner)
points: The Government appoints the MD & CEO and Executive Directors of public sector banks.
Public sector banks merged into fewer, bigger banks in 2019–2020; PNB absorbed two banks.
Big theme for interviews: public sector banks have cleaned up bad loans and now earn record profits.

numbers.say: PNB earned a record ₹16,904 crore in FY26 and has cut its bad loans to about 2.5%, showing a strong public sector turnaround.

rivals.note: Among public sector banks, PNB is third by FY26 profit after SBI and Bank of Baroda.

network.local: With deep roots in Punjab and North India, PNB is one of the biggest bank employers in the region, and new officers are often posted to rural and semi-urban branches.

employer.note: From the FY26 Directors' Report. PNB is a major public sector employer.

csr.t: PNB's CSR focuses on rural self-employment and farmer training, including 12 Farmers' Training Centres run by the PNB Farmers' Welfare Trust.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Amalgamation: Two or more companies combining into one. PNB absorbed Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India in 2020.
glossary.IBPS: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, which runs common recruitment exams for public sector banks.
glossary.MCLR: Marginal Cost of funds based Lending Rate: the base rate a bank uses to price many loans.

Personality, banking knowledge and HR questions

Finance.q: How did PNB cut Gross NPA from 3.95% to 2.95% in a year?
Finance.a: Better recoveries, write-offs of old bad loans and fewer new defaults, plus faster loan growth.

Finance.q: Why is PNB's margin lower than private banks'?
Finance.a: It has more low-yield government and corporate loans and higher-cost deposits; its global NIM was 2.58% in Q2 FY27.

Marketing.q: How would you attract young customers to PNB?
Marketing.a: Mobile-first account opening, student and first-salary accounts, and campaigns that mix the bank's trust with modern features.

Marketing.q: PNB signed a credit-card deal with the Indian Army. Why is that smart?
Marketing.a: It gives a large, stable customer base with regular salaries and builds loyalty.

HR.q: How would you prepare 96,000 employees for AI-led banking?
HR.a: Step-by-step digital training, champions in each zone, and showing staff how AI removes routine work.

Sales.q: Sell a PNB current account to a shopkeeper in a small town.
Sales.a: Ask about cash and UPI needs, then link QR collections, overdraft and a trusted government bank.

Operations.q: How would you speed up loan processing at a rural branch?
Operations.a: Digital KYC, pre-filled forms, business correspondents for document collection and tracking turnaround time.

interview.why_us: PNB was born in Punjab in 1894 with the vision of a truly Indian bank, and today it is a strong public sector bank with record profits of ₹16,904 crore and steadily falling bad loans. Its reach across North India means my work would touch families and small businesses in towns like mine. I want to grow with PNB and contribute to [your role].

gd.t: Were public sector bank mergers a good idea?
gd.for: Bigger banks like PNB now earn record profits and have stronger capital.
gd.against: Mergers caused staff and system integration problems for years.

gd.t: Should the government reduce its stake in public sector banks?
gd.for: More private investors can bring efficiency.
gd.against: Government ownership supports rural and social banking goals.

avoid: Don't call PNB a private bank; it is a public sector bank, about 70% owned by the government.
Don't say Oriental Bank of Commerce still exists separately; it merged into PNB in 2020.
Don't quote old bad-loan figures; Gross NPA is now 2.55% (Sep 2026).
